DELTA MODULATION (DM)
w Describe the characteristics of DM signals.
OBJECTIVES

w Describe the MC3418 DM demodulator integrated circuit....
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you are taught another method of digital signal processing and the circuits that modulate and demodulate.
INTRODUCTIONM
The method is called delta modulation, DM for short, after the Greek word delta meaning change.
Delta modulation is similar to pulse code modulation (PCM).
An information signal is changed to digital pulses and transmitted.
The digital pulses are received and changed back into the original information signal.
The difference, and an advantage over PCM, is that DM does not require a synchronization pulse and does not use A/D and D/A converters.
The disadvantage of DM is that it is not as accurate as PCM.
Consequently, DM is used mainly in voice communication systems where a perfect reproduction of the analog signal is not necessary.
Let's begin the lesson on DELTA MODULATION (DM)...........................

DELTA MODULATION SIGNALS
Delta modulation is a signal processing technique that produces a string of digital pulses according to how an information signal amplitude is changing.
DISCUSSION
In fact, the word DELTA is from the Greek word or letter (D) meaning a change..
The string of digital pulses represent increases and decreases in amplitude of an analog information signal, not a binary number.
What does the digital pulses in DM signal processing represent?
A signal that represents amplitude level is AM. The digital signal in DM does not represent amplitude levels.
TRY AGAIN!
A signal that represents frequency changes is FM. The digital signal in DM does not represent frequency changes.
TRY AGAIN!
One type of DM signal is called a POLARITY signal..........
When the information signal is increasing, positive pulses are generated. Times T1 and T3.
When the information signal is decreasing, negative pulses are generated. Time T2.
When the information signal is not changing, positive and negative pulses changing, positive and negative pulses are generated. Time T4.
The toggling action is due to an absence of a pulse for an information signal that does not change.
The 0 level of the DM signal only represents spacing between pulses.
The other type of DM signal is called a LEVEL signal.......
When the information signal is increasing, the DM signal is HIGH.
When the information signal is decreasing, the DM signal is LOW.
When the information signal is not changing, HIGH and LOW signals are generated. Time T4.
Like in the polarity DM signal, there is no signal for a constant information signal.
The DM signal toggles between the HIGH and LOW levels.

The position of pulses may appear to change but, that's not what DM changes. DM is delta modulation and delta means change.

To better understand DM signals, let's study the four basic characteristics starting with sampling.
As in any system that converts analog signals to digital, sampling must be used.
In the polarity method of DM, the sampling times are obvious.
Each pulse, positive or negative, represents a sample time.
In the Level Method of DM, the sampling times are not obvious.
As long as the information signal is increasing or decreasing, the DM signal remains HIGH or LOW, no pulses.
Only when the information signal changes between increasing or decreasing is the level of the pulse changed, at the sample time.
However, no matter the method of DM, the analog information signal must be sampled to determine if the information signal is increasing or decreasing in amplitude.
The minimum sample rate is the Nyquist rate or twice the highest information signal frequency.
Where fs is the sample rate and fmmax is the highest information signal frequency.y
If the sample rate is below the Nyquist rate, the demodulator circuit will not recover the information.
In a DM system using information signals that range from 10 kHz to 40 kHz, what is the minimum sample frequency that can be used?
20 kHz is twice the lowest frequency in the information signal. The minimum the information signal. The minimum frequency for sampling is twice the highest frequency in the information signal.
TRY AGAIN!
40 kHz is the highest frequency in the information signal. The minimum frequency for sampling is twice the highest in the information signal.
TRY AGAIN!
MINIMUM SAMPLING FREQUENCY - The minimum sampling frequency that can be used is the Nyquist rate. The Nyquist rate is defined as twice the highest information signal frequency.
The second characteristic of DM signals is Quantization....
DM systems do not have a quantization level as defined in PCM systems (no formula). DM systems do not use A/D and D/A converters.
Recall that in PCM systems, the quantization level was discrete voltage levels that were converted to digital.
In DM systems, the digital signals only represent changes, not discrete voltage levels.
However, the analog information signal is broken down into levels in the modulator depending on the sample rate and frequency of the information signal.
The levels are still called quantization levels but are not the same PCM quantization levels.
For example, the frequency of the left hand analog signal allows six levels at a given sample rate.
If the information signal increased, keeping the same shape and sample rate, the levels would be 3 as in the right hand signal.
There is actually no difference between the two DM signals, each one represents an increasing information signal.
The demodulator would produce the same output..............
And any differences in amplitude would be made up by using amplifier circuits.
Remember, the pulses only represent changes in the information signal, not discrete voltage levels.
The only important aspect of the levels, or q, is the quantization noise that is produced.
Recall in PCM systems, the quantization noise is the error caused by the discrete levels.
Analog signals have an infinite number of discrete levels, digital signals do not.
In DM systems, the quantization noise is also due to the levels, q, which as you know, depend on the frequency of the information signal and sample rate.
The more samples that are taken, more levels or q, the better the information signal is described.
Which produces less noise in the demodulator.
Of course, since the number of samples per cycle of the information signal depend on the information signal frequency, the noise or SNRq, varies.
There is no set formula for noise as there was in PCM.
The last characteristic is bandwidth and bandwidth is important in any type of communication system.
Bandwidth in DM systems is less than the bandwidth in PCM systems.
This can be critical in systems that have bandwidth restrictions.
Recall that the bandwidth in a PCM system is the sampling frequency times the number of bits in each frame.
Also note that it takes numerous frames to describe the simplest analog information signal.
However, in DM systems, there are no frames, the pulse train just represents changes in the analog signal.
Consequently, the bandwidth equals the sampling frequency.
What is the minimum bandwidth of a DM system that uses an information signal that varies between 5 kHz and 7 kHz?
The bandwidth of a DM system equals the sample rate. A sample rate of 4 kHz for a 5 to 7 kHz information signal is not correct.
TRY AGAIN!
The bandwidth of a DM system equals the sample rate. A sample rate of 2 kHz for a 5 to 7 kHz information signal is not correct.
TRY AGAIN!
BANDWIDTH - The bandwidth of a DM system equals the sample rate. The minimum sample rate of a DM system is twice the highest frequency of the information signal.
As you have seen, Delta modulation is a simpler method of signal processing than PCM. However, it is not as accurate.

DELTA MODULATION CIRCUITS
DM modulators normally use integrated circuits.............
DISCUSSION
In fact, a DM modulator uses one chip with only a few extra external components.
There are many types of DM chips. The one most often used is called a Continuous Variable Slope modulator, (CVSD, the D meaning Delta).
The CVSD chip develops a Level DM signal (highs and lows) and contains three major circuits.
The operation of the modulator is simple even though the circuits used inside the chip are complex.
The heart of the DM CVSD modulator is the integrator. Let's look at its operation.
An example of an integrator is a series RC circuit.........
With a high input, the capacitor charges according to the RC time constant.
The longer the high is applied, the greater the output voltage.
With a low input, the capacitor discharges according to the RC time constant.
The longer the low is applied, the less the output voltage.
The integrator circuit changes high and low inputs to an analog output signal.
And, the length of time that a high or low is applied determines the level of the analog output signal.
Returning to the CVSD circuit, the integrator output is applied to the negative input of the comparator.
The analog information signal is applied to the positive input of the comparator. The two inputs are then compared.
The comparator produces a high output if the analog input signal is greater than the integrator output signal.
The comparator produces a low output if the analog input signal is less than the integrator output signal.
The high or low output of the comparator is applied to the input of the integrator, making a closed loop.
The closed loop causes the analog output voltage of the integrator to follow the level of the analog information input signal.
In other words, the comparator compares the analog voltage from the integrator, which is delayed by circuit action, to the present analog input voltage.
When the present analog voltage is greater than the output of the integrator, it indicates that the input signal is increasing.
The output of the comparator is a high level as long as the analog information input signal is increasing.
When the present analog voltage is less than the output of the integrator, it indicates that the input signal is decreasing.
The output of the comparator is a low level as long as the analog information input signal is decreasing.
The output of the comparator are digital levels that indicate changes in the analog information input signal. DM modulation.
Note that if the the analog input signal is constant, the output of the comparator will toggle between high and low.
If the output of the integrator is greater than the analog input voltage, a low is produced.
The low output of the comparator decreases the integrator output voltage.
This will place the output of the integrator less than the input voltage producing a high comparator output.
The high output of the comparator increases the integrator output voltage.
This will place the output of the integrator greater than the input voltage producing a low comparator output.
The process continues producing a toggle output of the comparator.
Finally, the high or low output of the comparator is applied to a D type flip-flop.
On each clock pulse, which is the sample rate, the level on the D input sets or resets the flip-flop.
The output of the flip-flop is the Level DM signal.

DELTA DEMODULATION CIRCUITS
DM demodulators normally use integrated circuits...........
DISCUSSION
In fact, a DM demodulator can use the same type of chip used as a DM modulator.
Since level DM modulators are the most often used, a level demodulator will be studied.
The level DM demodulator changes highs and lows to analog and only consists of one major circuit.
The integrator circuit operates just like the integrator in DM modulators.
With a high input, the capacitor charges according to the RC time constant.
The longer the high is applied, the greater the output voltage.
With a low input, the capacitor discharges according to the RC time constant.
The longer the low is applied, the less the output voltage.
The integrator circuit changes high and low inputs, a level DM signal, to an analog output signal.
And the length of time that a high or low is applied determines the level of the analog output signal.
What type of circuit is used to demodulate a level DM signal?
A level DM demodulator circuit does not require a comparator.
TRY AGAIN!
A level DM demodulator circuit does not require a flip-flop..
TRY AGAIN!
What happens to the output signal of a level DM modulator if the input signal is low?
With a low input, the capacitor discharges in the integrator circuit lowering the output voltage.
TRY AGAIN!
The analog output of a level DM modulator will never stay the same. It will be increasing or decreasing according to the level of the input signal.
TRY AGAIN!
